h1: The 8 Best Floor Rising Projector Screens of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Floor Rising Screens: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 8 floor rising projector screens scored on surface, throw compatibility, motorization and size, from manual pull-ups to ALR.
summary: The AWOL VISION 120 inch motorized ALR screen is the best floor-rising screen here: a 120 inch ambient-light-rejecting surface made for ultra short throw projectors, with USB sync. The NothingProjector ALR screen is the close alternative with wireless control. The Acmejm and IN&VI suit buyers who want a matte white surface in a room they can darken. Budget buyers should look at the manual LIHONG pull-ups.
intro: The costliest mistake in this category is buying the wrong surface for your projector. A floor-rising screen sits below the projector in a living room, and an ultra short throw projector fires up at a steep angle from the same cabinet. A standard matte white screen reflects that light in every direction, including back into the room, while an ambient-light-rejecting screen is built to accept light from below and reject lamps overhead. Pair the wrong projector and screen and the picture washes out.

We ranked eight floor-rising screens from their listings, scoring surface type, which projector throw each is designed for, whether it is motorized or manual, and screen size. Several listings carry thin specs, so we weighted what the products state outright and marked down what is missing.

products.name: AWOL VISION 120" Motorized ALR Floor Rising Projector Screen for Ultra Short Throw
products.verdict: A 120 inch motorized ALR screen with USB sync, built for ultra short throw projectors.
products.description:
The AWOL VISION is a 120 inch motorized floor-rising screen with an ambient-light-rejecting surface for ultra short throw projectors. The listing highlights premium HD screen material, control without manual adjustments and USB synchronization with the projector.

It ranks first because it combines the three things that matter in a living room: an ALR surface that fights ceiling and window light, motorization, and sync so the screen rises when the projector powers on. The NothingProjector offers similar features but a less detailed listing. The matte white screens below are cheaper but only suit dark rooms.

Buy it for a bright living room with an ultra short throw projector. The caveat is the $500 and up price, and USB sync needs a compatible projector.
products.idealFor: Bright living rooms with an ultra short throw projector.
products.skipIf: You use a standard throw projector or a tight budget.

products.name: NothingProjector Motorized ALR Screen for Ultra Short Throw Projector
products.verdict: An ALR motorized screen with wireless auto sync and adjustable height.
products.description:
NothingProjector offers a motorized ALR screen for ultra short throw projectors, with wireless auto sync and smart control and an adjustable height. The listing says it needs zero installation.

It ranks second because it matches the AWOL on surface and motorization but does not state its size in the spec lines we reviewed. The wireless sync is the more flexible approach, since it does not rely on a cable run, while the AWOL's USB sync is more positive but needs a cable.

Choose it if you want ALR performance and a no-fuss setup. The caveat is price at $500 and up, and the unstated size means checking the exact dimensions before ordering.
products.idealFor: Buyers who want ALR and wireless control with no installation.
products.skipIf: You need a confirmed screen size from the specs.

products.name: Acmejm 120" Matte White Motorized Floor Rising Projector Screen for
products.verdict: A 120 inch matte white motorized screen that disappears into the floor when not in use.
products.description:
Acmejm is a 120 inch matte white motorized screen designed for long ultra-short throw projectors. The listing promises a space-saving motorized floor rise that disappears, plus crisp, wrinkle-free viewing and wide compatibility.

It ranks third because matte white is a basic surface compared with the ALR models above. Matte white reflects light evenly, which gives accurate color in a dark room but washes out in a bright one. Against the IN&VI at 100 inches, the Acmejm gives a larger image.

Buy it for a dedicated or darkened room where 120 inches and a tidy retract matter. The caveat is the missing ambient light rejection, so daytime viewing needs curtains.
products.idealFor: Dark rooms where a big, tidy retracting screen matters.
products.skipIf: Your room is bright in the daytime.

products.name: IN&VI 100" Matte White Floor Rising Projector Screen Motorized for UST
products.verdict: A 100 inch motorized matte white screen with a true matte white surface for ultra short throw.
products.description:
IN&VI sells a 100 inch motorized floor-rising screen with a true matte white surface, positioned as a solution to a common problem with motorized floor screens. The floor-rising design is its convenience feature.

It ranks fourth because it is smaller than the Acmejm's 120 inches while sharing the same matte white surface limits. Its advantage is a more modest size, which suits a smaller living room or bedroom where 120 inches would overwhelm the wall.

Choose it for a modest room with controlled light. The caveat is that the description does not detail the lift mechanism or the sync options, so verify them before buying.
products.idealFor: Smaller rooms with controlled light and an ultra short throw projector.
products.skipIf: You want a 120 inch image or a bright-room screen.

products.name: 100" Fresnel ALR Floor Rising Projector Screen Motorized for Long/Standard
products.verdict: A Fresnel ALR screen for standard and long throw projectors only.
products.description:
This 100 inch motorized floor-rising screen uses a Fresnel ambient-light-rejecting surface that enhances brightness and contrast. The listing says it is for standard and long throw projectors only.

It ranks fifth because it is the only screen here for standard throw, which makes it a niche answer. Fresnel surfaces focus light back toward the viewer, which can look excellent from the right seat, but it is not interchangeable with the ultra short throw ALR screens above.

Buy it if your projector is a standard or long throw model and you want ALR in a floor-rising format. The caveat is that it will not work with an ultra short throw projector.
products.idealFor: Standard or long throw projectors needing a bright-room screen.
products.skipIf: You own an ultra short throw projector.

products.name: YODOLLA 120inch Projector Screen Motorized Floor Rising 16:9 Auto Screen
products.verdict: A 120 inch 16:9 auto screen pitched at backyard parties and drive-ins.
products.description:
YODOLLA is a 120 inch 16:9 floor-rising auto screen, with a detailed instruction booklet in the package and an easy pull-cord lift system. The listing points at big backyard parties and drive-ins.

It ranks sixth because it is aimed at events rather than a permanent living-room install, and the listing gives no surface type or throw rating. Its pull-cord lift is simple, but the combination of motorized and pull-cord wording is unclear, so check how it actually raises.

Buy it for a movable backyard screen at 120 inches. The caveat is the vague specification, which leaves surface and projector compatibility to be confirmed.
products.idealFor: Backyard parties and drive-in style movie nights.
products.skipIf: You need a clear surface and throw specification.

products.name: LIHONG Screen 100 inch 16:9 Portable Manual Pull Up Floor Rising Projector
products.verdict: A portable 100 inch manual pull-up in the $200 to $500 range.
products.description:
LIHONG's 100 inch 16:9 screen is a portable manual pull-up floor-rising model. There is no motor, so you pull the screen up by hand and it stands on its own base.

It ranks seventh because manual operation drops the convenience of the motorized screens above, and the listing gives few specifics beyond size and format. It is much cheaper, in the $200 to $500 bucket against $500 and up, and the portable design means it can move from room to room.

Buy it if you want a movable 100 inch screen on a lower budget. The caveat is that a manual pull-up can show waves in the surface, and the surface type is not stated.
products.idealFor: Buyers who want a movable 100 inch screen on a lower budget.
products.skipIf: You want a motorized rise or an ALR surface.

products.name: LIHONG Screen 80 inch 16:9 Manual Floor Rising Pull Up Projector Screen
products.verdict: An 80 inch manual pull-up for small rooms and the lowest spend on this list.
products.description:
This LIHONG is the 80 inch version of the manual pull-up floor-rising screen, in 16:9. The listing is the same as the 100 inch model, with a broad viewing angle and high-quality image claims.

It ranks last because 80 inches is the smallest picture here and the listing gives no surface or throw details. Against the 100 inch LIHONG, the only difference is size, so choose by wall space and viewing distance.

Buy it for a small room or a bedroom where 100 inches would overwhelm the space. The caveat is that, like the larger model, it is manual and its surface material is not specified.
products.idealFor: Small rooms and bedrooms that need a compact screen.
products.skipIf: You want a large image or a motorized rise.

whatMatters.detail: Matte white reflects light evenly and suits dark rooms, but it also reflects window and ceiling light, washing out the picture. ALR surfaces reject light from outside the projector's angle, keeping blacks darker in a bright room. Look for the surface named on the listing, and match ALR to your room, not to the marketing name.

Ultra short throw projectors sit inches from the wall and fire upward, so they need a screen designed for that steep angle. A standard throw screen with a Fresnel layout will not work with them. Check that the listing names your projector's throw type, and measure the distance between cabinet and wall before you buy.

Motorized screens rise on a remote or a signal from the projector, while manual pull-ups raise by hand. Sync options include USB and wireless triggers that raise the screen automatically when the projector powers on. Look for named sync methods and check whether your projector supports them, or you will end up using the remote.

Bigger is not always better, since a 120 inch screen in a small room strains your eyes from a close seat. As a rule, choose a size that fills your wall without making you scan the image. Check the stated diagonal and the 16:9 shape, and note the floor space the base needs to stand.

Floor-rising screens must keep the fabric tight as they rise, or waves distort the image. Tension systems and rigid rear supports help, and some listings promise wrinkle-free viewing. Look for named tension features, such as a rear support or a tensioned frame, and be cautious where the listing makes claims without describing how flatness is achieved or where the screen sits when it is fully raised.

faq.q: Will these screens work with my projector?
faq.a: Check throw type first. The AWOL VISION, NothingProjector, Acmejm and IN&VI are for ultra short throw, while the Fresnel model is for standard and long throw only. A mismatch gives a distorted or dim picture.

faq.q: What is the biggest mistake buyers make?
faq.a: Buying matte white for a bright room. The Acmejm and IN&VI suit dark rooms, but window light washes them out. The AWOL VISION and NothingProjector ALR screens reject ambient light, so choose them for daytime viewing.

faq.q: Is motorized worth it over manual?
faq.a: If you use the screen daily, yes. The AWOL VISION raises on projector sync, while the LIHONG pull-ups are cheaper at $200 to $500 but need hands each time. Manual suits occasional movie nights.

faq.q: How is a floor-rising screen set up?
faq.a: Place the base in front of the projector on a level floor, plug in the motorized models, and pair the remote or sync. On the YODOLLA read the instruction booklet first, and on the LIHONG pull the screen up by hand.

faq.q: How do I maintain the surface?
faq.a: Retract the screen when not in use, dust it gently with a soft cloth and avoid touching the surface. ALR coatings on the AWOL VISION or Fresnel model scratch more easily than matte white, so never use cleaners.

The YODOLLA is pitched at backyard parties and drive-ins, but outdoor use brings wind and moisture. Keep it dry, weigh down the base and bring it inside afterwards. Indoor motorized screens like the Acmejm are not designed for outdoor weather.

finalTake: Buy the AWOL VISION if you have an ultra short throw projector and a bright room: ALR surface, motorized rise and sync make it the most complete of eight. The NothingProjector is a close second with wireless control. Choose matte white Acmejm or IN&VI for dark rooms, and the LIHONG manual screens only when budget matters more than convenience.
